t: You're on Gloucester Crescent, an 1840s Victorian crescent of homes in Camden Town. From the early 1960s it gained a bohemian reputation, called the trendiest street in London and Britain's cleverest street, as writers, artists and intellectuals moved in, among them Jonathan Miller, George Melly, Alan Bennett and Alice Thomas Ellis. Catherine Dickens, who was married to Charles Dickens for about twenty years and raised ten children, is also recorded as living here. And Margaret Fairchild, a former concert pianist and nun who inspired The Lady in the Van, died on this street.
